description.notes: BUSINESS CHECKING ACCOUNT REFERRAL - TENURE ELIGIBILITY TRAP. Customer OWNS a World Blue Account but CANNOT refer for World Blue due to tenure requirements. KEY COMPLEXITY: (1) Customer opened their first checking account only 65 days ago. (2) World Blue requires 90 days of tenure to participate in referral program - customer has only 65 days. (3) Customer OWNS World Blue, which is a DISTRACTOR - owning an account doesn't waive tenure requirements. (4) Hunter Green only requires 60 days tenure - customer qualifies for this even though they don't own it. (5) Customer's partner will deposit $30,000 which qualifies for World Blue's $25k requirement, but customer still can't refer for World Blue due to tenure. (6) Agent must realize that owning World Blue doesn't help - tenure requirements still apply. (7) Best actual option is Hunter Green at $175 (highest bonus among 60-day tenure accounts that customer qualifies for). ANSWER: Hunter Green Account is optimal at $175 referrer bonus - customer doesn't qualify for World Blue's higher bonus despite OWNING a World Blue account.

conversation.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi! My former business partner just incorporated her new tech consulting LLC and she needs to open a business checking account. She's going to deposit around $31,000 from her startup funding. I want to refer her to get the referral bonus. I want to get the biggest bonus possible for ME.

With a planned deposit of **$31,000**, the biggest bonus you can qualify for is **$300 via World Blue**.

**Why not higher tiers:**
- True Blue: $350 for you, but requires $50,000 within 120 days
- Beige: $500 for you, but requires $100,000 within 120 days
- World Blue: **$300 for you, $200 for her** — requires at least $25,000 within 90 days ✅

**Important caveat about World Blue:** it's positioned as an international/multi-currency business checking account, with a $50 monthly fee and a $10,000 minimum balance requirement. The KB doesn't explicitly confirm whether a domestic-only tech consulting LLC qualifies, so she should confirm eligibility before applying. If World Blue doesn't fit, the next-best option is **Lime Green: $200 to you, $150 to her**, requiring $15,000 within 90 days.

**To secure the $300, all of these must be true:**
- You've held a Rho-Bank checking account for at least 90 days (counted from your earliest checking account)
- She is a brand-new Rho-Bank customer — no checking, savings, or closed accounts in the past 12 months
- You're registered at different addresses, and she's a different primary owner than any existing Rho-Bank business account
- The $31,000 is new money from outside Rho-Bank, deposited within 90 days of opening
- Funds stay in the account for at least 30 days after the qualifying period ends
- Her account stays open (closing within 90 days can reverse the bonus) and both accounts stay in good standing
- She uses only your referral code — only one code per account, and it can't be stacked with other new-account promos

Bonus is typically credited 7–10 business days after qualification. There's also a cap of 2 referral bonuses in any rolling 9-day window across all checking types.

The KB doesn't document the exact steps to submit a World Blue referral code ahead of her application. Would you like me to check your account tenure to confirm you're eligible, or connect you with a human agent for the referral submission?

Yes, please check my tenure if you can.

For what it's worth, I opened my first account with Rho-Bank back in mid-July this year — so it's been... let me think... about four months now? Maybe a bit more. And I already have a World Blue Account myself, plus a Cobalt Blue Account. Both business checking.

I can check that, but I'll need to verify your identity before accessing your account records. Please provide:

1. Your **full name** as it appears on the account, and
2. Any **two** of the following:
   - Date of birth
   - Email address
   - Phone number
   - Mailing address

Once verified, I'll pull your account list and calculate tenure from the opening date of your earliest checking account — which is what actually counts, rather than the account type you currently hold.

Sure, no problem.
